end.summary:
Discussed the structure of district courts, High Courts, and the Supreme Court.
Practised the idea that a case may move from a district court to a High Court and then the Supreme Court through appeal.
Identified theft as a criminal case and distinguished it from a landlord-related civil matter.
Teach-back was not passed; Vihaan asked how people without money can access the Supreme Court.
end.parentNote: Vihaan practised court structure and appeals by explaining the path from district court to High Court to Supreme Court. They used examples from theft and landlord disputes; an initial mix-up about whether civil and criminal cases were part of the appeal path was clarified later by identifying theft as criminal and the landlord matter as civil. At home, ask them to draw the three-court appeal pathway and label one civil and one criminal example.
